claims.text: Untreated 316L components typically feature tensile residual stresses.
Laser shock peening under optimized parameters will induce compressive residual stresses in 316L stainless steel.
Laser shock peening will produce a compressively stressed surface layer.
Laser shock peening will refine grain boundaries in the treated surface layer.
Laser shock peening will increase dislocation density in the treated surface layer.
The compressive residual stresses produced by laser shock peening will extend deeply beneath the surface.
Laser-shock-peening-induced compressive residual stresses will retard crack initiation.
Laser-shock-peening-induced compressive residual stresses will retard crack propagation.
The refined surface microstructure will improve hardness.
The refined surface microstructure will improve resistance to stress-corrosion cracking.
Laser shock peening will significantly improve fatigue life relative to untreated 316L under identical conditions.
Laser shock peening will improve corrosion resistance relative to untreated 316L under identical conditions.
Laser shock peening will measurably increase surface hardness relative to untreated 316L.
Laser shock peening will reduce crack density relative to untreated material.
The benefits will remain effective under corrosive media, cyclic mechanical loading, and ambient to moderately elevated temperatures.
Careful optimization of laser energy density, overlap, and coverage is required to avoid surface microcracking or other processing-induced damage.
The benefits will be lost or diminished if operating temperatures exceed the range over which induced residual stresses remain stable.
